text:
anna-k: Quick follow-up after yesterday's attention-kernel RFC. I dug into the A100/H100/L4 pathing tradeoffs and sketched a fallback flow. TL;DR: prefer tiled-fused kernels on A100, fused-linear on H100, and simple fallback on L4. Thoughts?

devon: can you paste the flow? want to check the gating points (SM features vs. compute cap).

anna-k: pasted below. it's rough:

```
probe SM_features -> if(L2_atomic && tensorcore_bf16) -> route: fused_tiled (A100 path)
else if(matrix_core && sparse_support) -> route: fused_linear_block (H100 path)
else if(memory_bandwidth_low) -> route: simple_attention (L4 fallback)
fallback: run reference attention (single-threaded safe)
```

jia: hmm the `memory_bandwidth_low` heuristic worries me. on multitenant hosts bandwidth varies over time. we should prefer dynamic runtime probing (short micro-bench) instead of a static flag.

mike: +1 to runtime probe. also, for H100 we can enable larger tile sizes but need to guard TN layout assumptions. if we mis-detect layout we get wrong outputs. add a checksum verification after first batch.

anna-k: good call. propose: on first N requests (N=4) run selected kernel with checksum of first and last token outputs vs reference quantized kernel. if mismatch > threshold -> degrade to safer path and emit audit event.

devon: how expensive is the checksum? do we compare full tensors or a small hash sketch?

mike: small hash sketch (xxhash64) of KV slices should be enough. compute cost ~0.3ms per check on 80GB GPU, acceptable for cold start.

jia: need to wire this into rollout APIs. customers on Dedicated might want to opt out of checksum probes for strict p95 latency SLOs. add config: `kernel_probing { enabled: bool, sample_rate: 0.1, checksum: "xxhash64" }`

anna-k: agreed. also adding metric names: `kernel.probe.checksum.fail`, `kernel.route.selected`, `kernel.probe.latency_ms`. make them available in trace span for per-request debugging.

devon: for cap gating, we should prefer capability probing at startup + periodic re-probe on OOM/soft-failure. don't re-probe every request. maybe on every restart and on N consecutive failures.

mike: edge case — model with long context uses KV cache heavy writes. some fused kernels allocate transient buffers that push OOM on L4. we should simulate peak KV footprint during probe using window=2048 steps to catch that.

anna-k: i'll update the RFC appendix with: 1) startup probe sequence 2) N=4 verification, 3) sample checksum, 4) customer opt-out flag, 5) OOM re-probe policy, 6) telemetry names.

sre-bot: deploy-notes: please add a migration plan for Dedicated fleet to ensure probes don't cause mass evictions. recommended ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 100% over 48h with anomaly watch.

devon: thanks. can you add a short example config snippet for console UI? ops wants a toggle and sample-rate slider.

anna-k: sure, will post updated snippet in the RFC thread later today. :thumbsup:

jia: one more: document expected performance deltas (p50/p95) per GPU path in the appendix so product can set defaults. otherwise customers will be confused why H100 path is chosen but p95 worse for tiny batch workloads.

anna-k: noted. will add microbench table (batch sizes 1,4,8; seq len 128/512/2048) and include fallback thresholds.

mike: if no one objects i'll start prototyping the probe harness tomorrow (cc @devon).

devon: go for it. keep it behind a feature-flag for now.

anna-k: thanks all — closing this follow-up thread. I'll link the updated appendix once landed.
